# Chi2 likelihood {#sec-chi2_lrt}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}

$$
    \chi^2 = - 2(\log L_1 - \log L_0)
$${#eq-chi2-lrt}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Chi-square Likelihood Ratio Test for Comparing Nested Linear Models"
#| label: fig-chi2-lrt

# Create sample data
set.seed(999)
n <- 100
x1 <- rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1)
x2 <- rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1)
y <- -1 + 1.5*x1 + 0.8*x2 + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)  # linear response with noise

data <- data.frame(y = y, x1 = x1, x2 = x2)

# Fit two nested linear models
# Model 1 (reduced/null model): Only x1
model1 <- lm(y ~ x1, data = data)
print("Model 1 (Reduced): y ~ x1")
print(summary(model1))

# Model 2 (full/alternative model): x1 + x2
model2 <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data)
print("\nModel 2 (Full): y ~ x1 + x2")
print(summary(model2))

# Compare nested models using likelihood ratio test (F-test for linear models)
print("\nLikelihood Ratio Test: Model 1 vs Model 2")
lrt_result <- anova(model1, model2)
print(lrt_result)

# Extract test statistics
chi2_stat <- lrt_result$`F`[2]
p_value <- lrt_result$`Pr(>F)`[2]
df <- lrt_result$Df[2]

print(paste("F-statistic:", round(chi2_stat, 4)))
print(paste("p-value:", round(p_value, 4)))
print(paste("Numerator degrees of freedom:", df))

# Interpretation:
# If p-value > 0.05: we fail to reject H0 (reduced model is sufficient, x2 doesn't add significant information)
# If p-value < 0.05: we reject H0 (full model is better, x2 adds significant explanatory power)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Linear Model Comparison: RSS and Information Criteria"
#| label: fig-chi2-deviance

# Set up 1x2 panel layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Panel 1: Extract and compare residual sum of squares (RSS)
rss1 <- sum(residuals(model1)^2)
rss2 <- sum(residuals(model2)^2)

model_names <- c("Model 1\n(y ~ x1)", "Model 2\n(y ~ x1 + x2)")
rss_values <- c(rss1, rss2)

barplot(rss_values,
        names.arg = model_names,
        main = "Model Residual Sum of Squares Comparison",
        ylab = "RSS",
        col = c("lightcoral", "lightgreen"),
        border = "black",
        lwd = 1.5,
        ylim = c(0, max(rss_values) * 1.1))

# Add values on bars
text(1:2, rss_values + 1, round(rss_values, 2), ha = "center", cex = 1)

# Panel 2: AIC and BIC comparison
aic1 <- AIC(model1)
aic2 <- AIC(model2)
bic1 <- BIC(model1)
bic2 <- BIC(model2)

comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Model 1", "Model 2"),
  AIC = c(aic1, aic2),
  BIC = c(bic1, bic2)
)

# Create a grouped barplot
x_pos <- barplot(t(comparison[, c("AIC", "BIC")]),
                 names.arg = comparison$Model,
                 main = "Model Selection Criteria",
                 ylab = "Value",
                 col = c("steelblue", "coral"),
                 legend = TRUE,
                 beside = TRUE,
                 border = "black",
                 lwd = 1.5)

# Add values on bars
text(x_pos, c(aic1, aic2, bic1, bic2) + 1, round(c(aic1, aic2, bic1, bic2), 2), ha = "center", cex = 0.8)

# Reset plot layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
